title.zh: 卷二百六十八 列傳第一百五十六 曹文詔 周遇吉 黃得功
title.en: Volume 268 Biographies 156: Cao Wenzhao, Zhou Yuji, Huang Degong
title.raw: 卷二百六十八 列傳第一百五十六 曹文詔 周遇吉 黃得功 Volume 268 Biographies 156: Cao Wenzhao, Zhou Yuji, Huang Degong

sentences.zh: 曹文詔

translations.literal: Cao Wenzhao
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wenzhao

sentences.zh: 〈（弟文耀）〉

translations.literal: (his younger brother Wenyao)〉
translations.idiomatic: (his younger brother Wenyao)〉

sentences.zh: 周遇吉黃得功

translations.literal: Zhou Yuji Huang Degong
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yuji and Huang Degong

sentences.zh: 曹文詔，大同人。

translations.literal: Cao Wenzhao was a man of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wenzhao was a native of Datong.

sentences.zh: 勇毅有智略。

translations.literal: He was brave, resolute, and possessed of strategic ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and resolute, with a gift for strategy.

sentences.zh: 從軍遼左，歷事熊廷弼、孫承宗，積功至遊擊。

translations.literal: He joined the army in eastern Liaodong, served under Xiong Tingbi and Sun Chengzong, and through accumulated merit rose to the rank of guerrilla commander.
translations.idiomatic: He took service in eastern Liaodong under Xiong Tingbi and Sun Chengzong, and by steady achievement advanced to guerrilla commander.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年冬，從袁崇煥入衛京師。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Chongzhen, he followed Yuan Chonghuan in coming to defend the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Chongzhen 2 (1629), he marched with Yuan Chonghuan to the capital's defense.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，總理馬世龍畀所賜尚方劍，令率參將王承胤、張叔嘉、都司左良玉等伏玉田、枯樹、洪橋，鏖戰有功，遷參將。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, the supreme commander Ma Shilong gave him the imperial sword he had received and ordered him to lead the assistant generals Wang Chengyin, Zhang Shujia, the regional commander Zuo Liangyu, and others in ambush at Yutian, Kushu, and Hongqiao; he fought fiercely with merit and was promoted to assistant general.
translations.idiomatic: The next February, supreme commander Ma Shilong entrusted him with the imperial sword he had been granted and sent him, with assistant generals Wang Chengyin and Zhang Shujia and regional commander Zuo Liangyu, to lie in wait at Yutian, Kushu, and Hongqiao. After fierce fighting with notable success, he was promoted to assistant general.

sentences.zh: 自大塹山轉戰逼遵化，又從世龍等克大安城及鮎魚諸關。

translations.literal: From Dachanshan he fought in succession pressing toward Zunhua, and again followed Shilong and others in capturing Da'an City and the Catfish Passes and other passes.
translations.idiomatic: He fought his way from Dachanshan toward Zunhua, then joined Shilong in taking Da'an City and the Catfish Passes.

sentences.zh: 以與復四城功，加都督僉事。

translations.literal: For his merit in recovering the four cities, he was given the additional title of vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: For helping recover the four cities, he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 七月，陜西賊熾，擢延綏東路副總兵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, when bandits in Shaanxi grew fierce, he was promoted to deputy commander of the eastern route in Yansui.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, with Shaanxi rebels raging, he was appointed deputy commander on Yansui's eastern front.

sentences.zh: 賊渠王嘉胤久據河曲。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftain Wang Jiayin had long held Hequ.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Wang Jiayin had long held Hequ.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，文詔克其城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, Wenzhao captured his city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Chongzhen 4, Wenzhao took the city.

sentences.zh: 嘉胤脫走，轉掠至陽城南山。

translations.literal: Jiayin escaped and turned to plunder as far as the southern hills of Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayin slipped away and raided south into the Yangcheng hills.

sentences.zh: 文詔追及之，其下斬以降，以功擢臨洮總兵官。

translations.literal: Wenzhao overtook him; his followers beheaded him to surrender, and for this merit Wenzhao was promoted to commander at Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao ran him down; his men killed him to surrender, and Wenzhao was made commander at Lintao for the victory.

sentences.zh: 點燈子自陜入山西。

translations.literal: Dian Dengzi entered Shanxi from Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel called Lamp-Lighter crossed from Shaanxi into Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 文詔追之，及於稷山，諭降七百人。

translations.literal: Wenzhao pursued him, caught up at Jishan, and persuaded seven hundred to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao pursued him to Jishan and induced seven hundred men to surrender.

sentences.zh: 點燈子遁，尋被獲，伏誅。

translations.literal: Dian Dengzi fled, was soon captured, and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Lamp-Lighter escaped but was soon taken and put to death.

sentences.zh: 李老柴、獨行狼陷中部，巡撫練國事、延綏總兵王承恩圍之。

translations.literal: Li Laochai and Lone Wolf had overrun the central region; the grand coordinator Lian Guoshi and the Yansui commander Wang Chengen besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Laochai and Lone Wolf had seized the central region; grand coordinator Lian Guoshi and Yansui commander Wang Chengen laid siege to them.

sentences.zh: 五月，慶陽賊郝臨庵、劉道江援之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Qingyang bandits Hao Lin'an and Liu Daojiang came to their relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the Qingyang rebels Hao Lin'an and Liu Daojiang marched to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 會文詔西旋，與榆林參政張福臻合剿，馘老柴及其黨一條龍，余黨奔摩雲谷。

translations.literal: Wenzhao happened to be returning west and, joining with the Yulin administrator Zhang Fuzhen in a joint campaign, beheaded Laochai and his follower One Dragon; the rest fled to Moyun Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao was then marching west; with Yulin administrator Zhang Fuzhen he struck jointly, killed Laochai and his lieutenant One Dragon, and drove the survivors toward Moyun Valley.

sentences.zh: 副將張弘業、遊擊李明輔戰死。

translations.literal: The deputy commander Zhang Hongye and the guerrilla commander Li Mingfu died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Zhang Hongye and guerrilla commander Li Mingfu were killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 文詔乃與遊擊左光先、崔宗蔭、李國奇分剿綏德、宜君、清澗、米脂賊，戰懷寧川、黑泉峪、封家溝、綿湖峪，皆大捷，掃地王授首。

translations.literal: Wenzhao then, with the guerrilla commanders Zuo Guangxian, Cui Zongyin, and Li Guoqi, divided forces to suppress bandits in Suide, Yijun, Qingjian, and Mizhi, fighting at Huaining River, Heiquan Ravine, Fengjia Gully, and Mianhu Ravine—all great victories—and the Sweeping-Earth King was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao then split his guerrilla commanders Zuo Guangxian, Cui Zongyin, and Li Guoqi against rebels in Suide, Yijun, Qingjian, and Mizhi. Victories at Huaining River, Heiquan Ravine, Fengjia Gully, and Mianhu Ravine followed, and the rebel called Sweeping-Earth King lost his head.

sentences.zh: 紅軍友、李都司、杜三、楊老柴者，神一魁余黨也，屯鎮原，將犯平涼。

translations.literal: Red Army Friend, Li Dusi, Du San, and Yang Laochai were remnant followers of Shen Yikui; they encamped at Zhenyuan and were about to attack Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Red Army Friend, Li Dusi, Du San, and Yang Laochai were survivors of Shen Yikui's band; encamped at Zhenyuan, they were poised to strike Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 國事檄甘肅總兵楊嘉謨、副將王性善扼之，賊走慶陽。

translations.literal: Guoshi ordered the Gansu commander Yang Jiamo and the deputy commander Wang Xingshan to block them, and the bandits fled to Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guoshi ordered Gansu commander Yang Jiamo and deputy Wang Xingshan to block them, and the rebels withdrew toward Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 文詔從鄜州間道與嘉謨、性善合。

translations.literal: Wenzhao came by a secret route from Fuzhou and joined Jiamo and Xingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao marched by a hidden route from Fuzhou and united with Jiamo and Xingshan.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，大戰西濠，斬千級，生擒杜三、楊老柴。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year they fought a great battle at Xihào, beheading a thousand, and took Du San and Yang Laochai alive.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Chongzhen 5 they fought a major battle at West Moat, killing a thousand men and capturing Du San and Yang Laochai alive.

sentences.zh: 余黨糾他賊掠武安監，陷華亭，攻莊浪。

translations.literal: The remaining followers gathered other bandits to plunder Wu'an Post, captured Huating, and attacked Zhuanglang.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors rallied other rebels, raided Wu'an Post, took Huating, and assaulted Zhuanglang.

sentences.zh: 文詔、嘉謨至，賊屯張麻村。

translations.literal: When Wenzhao and Jiamo arrived, the bandits were encamped at Zhangma Village.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzhao and Jiamo arrived, the rebels were holding Zhangma Village.

sentences.zh: 官軍掩擊，賊走高山。

translations.literal: The government troops struck by surprise, and the bandits fled to the high hills.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops struck from cover and drove the rebels into the high hills.

sentences.zh: 遊擊曹變蛟、馮舉、劉成功、平安等噪而上，賊潰走。

translations.literal: The guerrilla commanders Cao Bianjiao, Feng Ju, Liu Chenggong, Ping An, and others charged up with a shout, and the bandits broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Guerrilla commanders Cao Bianjiao, Feng Ju, Liu Chenggong, and Ping An led a shouting charge uphill, and the rebels broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 變蛟者，文詔從子也。

translations.literal: Bianjiao was Wenzhao's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Bianjiao was Wenzhao's nephew.

sentences.zh: 會性善及甘肅副將李鴻嗣、參將莫與京等至，共擊斬五百二十余級。

translations.literal: When Xingshan and the Gansu deputy commander Li Hongsi, the assistant general Mo Yujing, and others arrived, they fought together and beheaded more than five hundred twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshan arrived with Gansu deputy Li Hongsi and assistant general Mo Yujing; together they killed more than five hundred twenty rebels.

sentences.zh: 追敗之鹹寧關，又敗之關上嶺。

translations.literal: They pursued and defeated them at Xianning Pass and again defeated them at Guanshang Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued and routed them at Xianning Pass and again at Guanshang Ridge.

sentences.zh: 追至隴安，嘉謨、變蛟夾擊，復敗之。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Long'an, Jiamo and Bianjiao attacked from both sides and defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: At Long'an, Jiamo and Bianjiao caught them in a pincer and defeated them once more.

sentences.zh: 賊余眾數千欲走漢南，為遊擊趙光遠所遏，乃由長寧驛走張家川。

translations.literal: Several thousand remaining bandits wished to flee south of the Han River but were blocked by the guerrilla commander Zhao Guangyuan; they therefore went by Changning Post toward Zhangjiachuan.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand survivors tried to flee south of the Han but guerrilla commander Zhao Guangyuan blocked them, so they turned by Changning Post toward Zhangjiachuan.

sentences.zh: 其逸出清水者，副將蔣一陽遇之敗，都司李宮用被執。

translations.literal: Those who slipped out at Qingshui were met and defeated by the deputy commander Jiang Yiyang, but the regional commander Li Gongyong was captured.
translations.idiomatic: A band that slipped out at Qingshui was beaten by deputy Jiang Yiyang, though regional commander Li Gongyong was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 文詔乃縱反間，紿其黨，殺紅軍友，遂蹙敗之水落城。

translations.literal: Wenzhao then spread counter-intelligence, deceived their followers, had Red Army Friend killed, and thus cornered and defeated them at Shuiluo City.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao sowed discord among them, tricked their followers into killing Red Army Friend, then cornered the rest and crushed them at Shuiluo City.

sentences.zh: 追至靜寧州，賊奔據唐毛山，變蛟先登，殄其眾。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Jingning Prefecture, the bandits fled to hold Tangmao Mountain; Bianjiao was first to ascend and annihilated their force.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit reached Jingning, where the rebels fled to Tangmao Mountain; Bianjiao was first up the slope and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 可天飛、郝臨庵，劉道江為王承恩所敗，退保鐵角城。

translations.literal: Ketianfei, Hao Lin'an, and Liu Daojiang were defeated by Wang Chengen and withdrew to hold Iron Horn City.
translations.idiomatic: Ketianfei, Hao Lin'an, and Liu Daojiang, beaten by Wang Chengen, fell back to Iron Horn City.

sentences.zh: 獨行狼、李都司走與合，可天飛、劉道江遂圍合水。

translations.literal: Lone Wolf and Li Dusi fled to join them, and Ketianfei and Liu Daojiang then besieged Heshui.
translations.idiomatic: Lone Wolf and Li Dusi joined them, and Ketianfei and Liu Daojiang laid siege to Heshui.

sentences.zh: 文詔往救。

translations.literal: Wenzhao went to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao marched to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 賊匿精銳，以千騎逆戰，誘抵南原，伏大起。

translations.literal: The bandits hid their elite troops, met him with a thousand horsemen, lured him to the southern plain, and then their ambush rose in force.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hid their best troops, met him with a thousand horsemen, drew him onto the southern plain, and then sprang a great ambush.

sentences.zh: 城上人言曹將軍已歿。

translations.literal: Those on the walls said General Cao was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Men on the walls cried that General Cao was already dead.

sentences.zh: 文詔持矛左右突，匹馬縈萬眾中。

translations.literal: Wenzhao grasped his spear and charged left and right, a single horse threading through ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao levelled his spear and charged to and fro, one horse threading through a host of ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 諸軍望見，夾擊，賊大敗，僵屍蔽野，余走銅川橋。

translations.literal: The armies saw him and attacked from both sides; the bandits were utterly defeated, corpses covered the field, and the remainder fled to Tongchuan Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The troops saw him and closed in from both flanks; the rebels were routed, the field strewn with dead, and the survivors fled toward Tongchuan Bridge.

sentences.zh: 文詔率變蛟、舉、嘉謨及參將方茂功等追及之，大戰陷陣，賊復大敗。

translations.literal: Wenzhao led Bianjiao, Ju, Jiamo, and the assistant general Fang Maogong and others in pursuit, fought a great battle breaking into their ranks, and the bandits were again utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao pursued with Bianjiao, Ju, Jiamo, and assistant general Fang Maogong, fought through their lines, and routed them again.

sentences.zh: 尋與寧夏總兵賀虎臣、固原總兵楊麒破賊甘泉之虎兕凹。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, with the Ningxia commander He Huchen and the Guyuan commander Yang Qi, he defeated the bandits at Tiger-and-Rhino Hollow in Ganquan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he joined Ningxia commander He Huchen and Guyuan commander Yang Qi in defeating the rebels at Tiger-and-Rhino Hollow in Ganquan.

sentences.zh: 麒復追賊安口河、崇信窯、白茅山，皆大獲。

translations.literal: Qi again pursued the bandits at Ankou River, Chongxin Kiln, and Baimao Mountain, gaining great spoils each time.
translations.idiomatic: Qi pursued them further at Ankou River, Chongxin Kiln, and Baimao Mountain, winning major victories at each place.

sentences.zh: 總督洪承疇斬可天飛、李都司於平涼，降其將白廣恩，余賊分竄。

translations.literal: The governor-general Hong Chengchou beheaded Ketianfei and Li Dusi at Pingliang, accepted the surrender of their general Bai Guang'en, and the remaining bandits scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Hong Chengchou executed Ketianfei and Li Dusi at Pingliang, accepted the surrender of their general Bai Guang'en, and the remaining rebels scattered.

sentences.zh: 文詔追擊之隴州、平、鳳間。

translations.literal: Wenzhao pursued them between Longzhou, Pingliang, and Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao pursued them through the country between Longzhou, Pingliang, and Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 十月三戰三敗之，遂蹙賊耀州錐子山，其黨殺獨行狼、郝臨庵以降。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he fought three battles and defeated them three times, then cornered the bandits on Awl Mountain in Yaozhou; their followers killed Lone Wolf and Hao Lin'an to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he fought three times and won three times, then drove the rebels onto Awl Mountain in Yaozhou, where their men killed Lone Wolf and Hao Lin'an to surrender.

sentences.zh: 承疇戮四百人，余散遣。

translations.literal: Chengchou executed four hundred men and dispersed the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou executed four hundred men and sent the rest away.

sentences.zh: 關中巨寇略平。

translations.literal: The great bandits of Guanzhong were largely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The great rebel bands of Guanzhong were largely subdued.

sentences.zh: 巡撫御史範復粹匯奏首功凡三萬六千六百有奇，文詔功第一，嘉謨次之，承恩、麒又次之。

translations.literal: The censor-grand coordinator Fan Fucui submitted a consolidated report of heads taken totaling more than thirty-six thousand six hundred; Wenzhao's merit ranked first, Jiamo's second, and Chengen's and Qi's after that.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-grand coordinator Fan Fucui reported a combined head count of more than 36,600; Wenzhao ranked first in merit, Jiamo second, Chengen and Qi after them.

sentences.zh: 文詔在陜西，大小數十戰，功最多，承疇不為敘。

translations.literal: Wenzhao in Shaanxi fought several dozen battles large and small and achieved the most merit, but Chengchou did not record it.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaanxi Wenzhao fought dozens of engagements and won the greatest credit, yet Chengchou omitted him from the honors list.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史吳甡推獎甚至，復粹疏復上。

translations.literal: The touring censor Wu Shen praised him to the utmost, and Fucui memorialized again on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censor Wu Shen commended him in the strongest terms, and Fucui submitted another memorial on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 兵部抑其功，卒不敘。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War suppressed his merit, and in the end he received no reward.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War downgraded his credit, and in the end he received no reward.

sentences.zh: 當是時，賊見陜兵盛，多流入山西，其魁紫金梁、混世王、姬關鎖、八大王、曹操、闖塌天、興加哈利七大部，多者萬人，少亦半之，蹂躪汾州、太原、平陽。

translations.literal: At this time, seeing Shaanxi troops strong, the bandits mostly flowed into Shanxi; their chiefs—Purple-Gold Beam, World-Wrecker King, Ji Guansuo, Eight Great Kings, Cao Cao, Rush-the-Sky, Xing Jiaha Li—and seven great hosts, the larger with ten thousand men and the smaller half that, ravaged Fenzhou, Taiyuan, and Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Shaanxi's armies strong, most rebels poured into Shanxi under seven major chiefs—Purple-Gold Beam, World-Wrecker King, Ji Guansuo, Eight Great Kings, Cao Cao, Rush-the-Sky, and Xing Jiaha Li—hosts of up to ten thousand men or half that, ravaging Fenzhou, Taiyuan, and Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 御史張宸極言：「賊自秦中來。

translations.literal: The censor Zhang Chenji said: "The bandits come from Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Chenji said: "These rebels come from Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦將曹文詔威名宿著，士民為之謠曰『軍中有一曹，西賊聞之心膽搖』。

translations.literal: The Qin general Cao Wenzhao's renown is long established; soldiers and people have a rhyme for him: 'In the army there is a Cao—western bandits hear it and their hearts and gall tremble.'
translations.idiomatic: The Qin general Cao Wenzhao's fame is long established; soldiers and civilians have a rhyme: 'In the army there is a Cao—western rebels hear it and their hearts shake.'

sentences.zh: 且嘗立功晉中，而秦賊滅且盡。

translations.literal: Moreover he has already achieved merit in Jin, and the Qin bandits were nearly all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: He has already distinguished himself in Jin, and the Qin rebels were nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 宜敕令入晉協剿。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to order him to enter Jin and join in the suppression campaign."
translations.idiomatic: He should be ordered into Jin to join the suppression campaign."

sentences.zh: 於是命陜西、山西諸將並受文詔節制。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered all generals of Shaanxi and Shanxi alike to accept Wenzhao's command.
translations.idiomatic: The court then placed all Shaanxi and Shanxi generals under Wenzhao's command.

sentences.zh: 六年正月抵霍州，敗賊汾河、盂系，追及於壽陽。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year he reached Huozhou, defeated bandits on the Fen River and in the Yu cluster, and overtook them at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Chongzhen 6 he reached Huozhou, defeated rebels on the Fen River and around Yu, and overtook them at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 巡撫許鼎臣遣謀士張宰先大軍嘗賊，賊驚潰。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator Xu Dingchen sent the strategist Zhang Zai ahead of the main army to probe the bandits, and the bandits fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Xu Dingchen sent strategist Zhang Zai ahead of the main force to probe the rebels, and they broke in panic.

sentences.zh: 二月，文詔追擊之，斬混世王於碧霞村。

translations.literal: In the second month Wenzhao pursued them and beheaded World-Wrecker King at Bixia Village.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Wenzhao pursued them and killed World-Wrecker King at Bixia Village.

sentences.zh: 余黨為猛如虎逐走，遇文詔兵方山，復敗。

translations.literal: The remaining followers were driven off by Meng Ru Hu and, meeting Wenzhao's troops at Fangshan, were defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors were harried by Meng Ru Hu, met Wenzhao at Fangshan, and were beaten again.

sentences.zh: 五臺、盂、定襄、壽陽賊盡平。

translations.literal: The bandits of Wutai, Yu, Dingxiang, and Shouyang were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels in Wutai, Yu, Dingxiang, and Shouyang were all subdued.

sentences.zh: 鼎臣命文詔軍平定，備太原東，張應昌軍汾州，備太原西。

translations.literal: Dingchen ordered Wenzhao's army to garrison Pingding and guard the east of Taiyuan, and Zhang Yingchang's army at Fenzhou to guard the west of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dingchen stationed Wenzhao at Pingding to guard Taiyuan's east and Zhang Yingchang at Fenzhou to guard its west.

sentences.zh: 文詔連敗賊太谷、範村、榆社，太原賊幾盡。

translations.literal: Wenzhao defeated the bandits in succession at Taigu, Fancun, and Yushe, and the Taiyuan bandits were nearly all gone.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao defeated rebels in turn at Taigu, Fancun, and Yushe, and the Taiyuan rebels were nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 帝以文詔功多，敕所過地多積糗糧以犒，並敕文詔速平賊。

translations.literal: Because Wenzhao's merits were many, the emperor ordered the places he passed to store up much grain and dry provisions to reward the troops, and also ordered Wenzhao to pacify the bandits quickly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, noting Wenzhao's many victories, ordered districts along his route to stock grain and provisions for his men and commanded him to finish off the rebels quickly.

sentences.zh: 山西監視中官劉中允言文詔剿賊徐溝、盂、定襄，所司不給米，反以炮石傷士卒。

translations.literal: The Shanxi supervising eunuch Liu Zhongyun said that when Wenzhao suppressed bandits at Xugou, Yu, and Dingxiang, the local offices gave no rice and instead wounded soldiers with cannon stones.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanxi supervising eunuch Liu Zhongyun reported that during Wenzhao's campaigns at Xugou, Yu, and Dingxiang, local officials withheld rations and even struck his men with artillery stones.

sentences.zh: 帝即下御史按問。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately sent censors to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once sent censors to investigate.

sentences.zh: 三月，賊從河內上太行，文詔大敗之澤州。

translations.literal: In the third month the bandits ascended the Taihang from Henei, and Wenzhao utterly defeated them at Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month rebels climbed the Taihang from Henei; Wenzhao routed them at Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 賊走潞安，文詔至陽城遇賊不擊，自沁水潛師，還擊之芹地、劉村寨，斬首千余。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to Lu'an; Wenzhao reached Yangcheng, met the bandits but did not strike, secretly moved his army from Qinshui, and struck them in return at Qindi and Liucunzhai, beheading more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled toward Lu'an; at Yangcheng Wenzhao let them pass, then marched secretly from Qinshui and struck them at Qindi and Liucunzhai, taking more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 四月，賊屯潤城，其他部陷平順，殺知縣徐明揚。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the bandits encamped at Runcheng; another band captured Pingshun and killed the magistrate Xu Mingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month rebels held Runcheng while another band took Pingshun and killed magistrate Xu Mingyang.

sentences.zh: 文詔至，賊走，乃夜半襲潤城，斬賊千五百。

translations.literal: When Wenzhao arrived the bandits fled; he then raided Runcheng at midnight and beheaded fifteen hundred bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzhao arrived the rebels fled; he raided Runcheng at midnight and killed fifteen hundred of them.

sentences.zh: 紫金梁、老回回自榆社走武鄉，過天星走高澤山，文詔皆擊敗。

translations.literal: Purple-Gold Beam and Old Huihui fled from Yushe toward Wuxiang; Guo Tianxing went toward Gaozeshan; Wenzhao defeated them all.
translations.idiomatic: Purple-Gold Beam and Old Huihui fled from Yushe toward Wuxiang, and Guo Tianxing toward Gaozeshan; Wenzhao defeated them all.

sentences.zh: 他賊圍涉縣，聞文詔破賊黎城，解去。

translations.literal: Other bandits besieged She County; hearing that Wenzhao had defeated bandits at Licheng, they lifted the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: Other rebels were besieging She County; when they heard Wenzhao had beaten the band at Licheng, they raised the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五月，帝遣中官孫茂霖為文詔內中軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the emperor sent the eunuch Sun Maolin to serve as Wenzhao's inner staff commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor assigned eunuch Sun Maolin as Wenzhao's inner staff commander.

sentences.zh: 賊犯沁水，文詔大敗之，擒其魁大虎，又敗之遼城毛嶺山西。

translations.literal: The bandits attacked Qinshui; Wenzhao utterly defeated them, captured their chieftain Big Tiger, and again defeated them west of Maoling in Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels struck Qinshui; Wenzhao routed them, captured their chief Big Tiger, and beat them again west of Maoling in Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 賊既屢敗，乃避文詔鋒，多流入河北。

translations.literal: The bandits, having been repeatedly defeated, therefore avoided Wenzhao's edge and mostly flowed into Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly beaten, the rebels avoided Wenzhao's front and mostly poured into Hebei.

sentences.zh: 帝乃命文詔移師往討。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Wenzhao to move his army to campaign there.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Wenzhao to march there to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 而賊已敗鄧玘兵於林縣，文詔率五營軍夜襲破之。

translations.literal: But the bandits had already defeated Deng Yin's troops at Lin County; Wenzhao led the five-camp army in a night raid and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already beaten Deng Yin's force at Lin County; Wenzhao led five camps in a night attack and routed them.

sentences.zh: 七月大敗懷慶賊柴陵村，馘其魁滾地龍，又追斬老回回於濟源。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he utterly defeated the Huaqing bandits at Chailing Village, beheaded their chieftain Rolling Earth Dragon, and again pursued and beheaded Old Huihui at Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he routed the Huaqing rebels at Chailing Village, killed their chief Rolling Earth Dragon, and pursued Old Huihui to Jiyuan and killed him.

sentences.zh: 文詔在洪洞時，與裏居御史劉令譽忤。

translations.literal: When Wenzhao was at Hongtong, he had a falling-out with the retired censor Liu Lingyu.
translations.idiomatic: While stationed at Hongtong, Wenzhao had quarreled with retired censor Liu Lingyu.

sentences.zh: 及是，令譽按河南，而四川石矽土官馬鳳儀軍敗沒於侯家莊，賴文詔馳退賊。

translations.literal: At this time Lingyu was touring Henan, while in Sichuan the native-official Ma Fengyi of the Shiqi tribe had his army destroyed at Houjiazhuang; it was thanks to Wenzhao's rapid march that the bandits were driven off.
translations.idiomatic: Now Lingyu was inspecting Henan; in Sichuan the Shiqi native-official Ma Fengyi's army was wiped out at Houjiazhuang, and only Wenzhao's swift advance drove the rebels back.

sentences.zh: 甫解甲，與令譽相見，語復相失。

translations.literal: He had just laid aside his armor when he met Lingyu; their words again clashed.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely doffed his armor when he met Lingyu, and their words clashed again.

sentences.zh: 文詔拂衣起，面叱之。

translations.literal: Wenzhao flung his robe and rose, rebuking him to his face.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao flung his robe aside, rose, and rebuked him to his face.

sentences.zh: 令譽怒，遂以鳳儀之敗為文詔罪。

translations.literal: Lingyu was enraged and therefore made Fengyi's defeat Wenzhao's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Lingyu blamed Wenzhao for Fengyi's defeat.

sentences.zh: 部議文詔怙勝而騎，乃調之大同。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated that Wenzhao, relying on victory, was arrogant, and transferred him to Datong.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry ruled that Wenzhao had grown arrogant on his victories and transferred him to Datong.

sentences.zh: 七年七月，大清兵西征插漢，還師入大同境，攻拔得勝堡、參將李全自經，遂攻圍懷仁縣及井坪堡、應州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventh year the Great Qing army campaigned west against Chahar, and on its return entered Datong territory, captured Desheng Fort, the assistant general Li Quan hanged himself, and they then attacked and besieged Huairen County as well as Jingping Fort and Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Chongzhen 7 the Qing army marched west against Chahar; on the return it entered Datong, took Desheng Fort—assistant general Li Quan hanged himself—and besieged Huairen County, Jingping Fort, and Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 文詔偕總督張宗衡先駐懷仁固守。

translations.literal: Wenzhao, together with the governor-general Zhang Zongheng, first stationed at Huairen to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao and governor-general Zhang Zongheng took post at Huairen and held the city.

sentences.zh: 八月，圍解，即移駐鎮城，挑戰敗還。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the siege was lifted; he then moved to garrison Zhencheng, offered battle, was defeated, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the siege lifted; he moved to Zhencheng, offered battle, was beaten, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 已而靈丘及他屯堡多失陷，大清兵亦旋。

translations.literal: Before long Lingqiu and many other garrison forts fell, and the Great Qing army also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lingqiu and many other forts fell, and the Qing army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十一月論罪，文詔、宗衡及巡撫胡沾恩並充軍邊衛。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month guilt was assessed; Wenzhao, Zongheng, and the grand coordinator Hu Zhan'en were all sentenced to military exile on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month all three were punished: Wenzhao, Zongheng, and grand coordinator Hu Zhan'en were sentenced to frontier military exile.

sentences.zh: 令甫下，山西巡撫吳甡薦文詔知兵善戰，請用之晉中。

translations.literal: The order had just been issued when the Shanxi grand coordinator Wu Shen recommended Wenzhao as knowing warfare and skilled in battle, asking that he be used in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The order had barely been issued when Shanxi grand coordinator Wu Shen recommended Wenzhao as a skilled commander and asked that he be used in Jin.

sentences.zh: 乃命為援剿總兵官，立功自贖。

translations.literal: He was then appointed relief-suppression commander-in-chief, to redeem himself through merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed relief-suppression commander-in-chief, to redeem himself through merit.

sentences.zh: 當是時，河南禍尤劇，帝已允兵部議，敕文詔馳剿河南賊。

translations.literal: At this time the disaster in Henan was especially severe; the emperor had already approved the Ministry of War's deliberation and ordered Wenzhao to hurry to suppress the Henan bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Henan's crisis was especially grave; the emperor had approved the ministry's plan and ordered Wenzhao to rush south against the Henan rebels.

sentences.zh: 甡復抗疏力爭，請令先平晉賊，後入豫，帝不許。

translations.literal: Shen again submitted a defiant memorial arguing forcefully, asking that he first pacify the Jin bandits and only afterward enter Yu; the emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shen submitted another forceful memorial asking that Wenzhao finish the Shanxi rebels before entering Henan; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 而文詔以甡有恩，竟取道太原，為甡所留。

translations.literal: But Wenzhao, owing Shen a debt of gratitude, actually took the route through Taiyuan and was detained by Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful to Wu Shen, Wenzhao took the road through Taiyuan and was kept there by him.

sentences.zh: 會賊高加計已殲，而鳳陽告陷，遂整兵南，以八年三月會總督洪承疇於信陽。

translations.literal: It happened that the bandit Gao Jiaji had already been destroyed, but Fengyang reported its fall; he therefore arrayed his troops southward and in the third month of the eighth year joined the governor-general Hong Chengchou at Xinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiaji's band was already destroyed, but Fengyang had fallen; Wenzhao marched south and in the third month of Chongzhen 8 joined Hong Chengchou at Xinyang.

sentences.zh: 承疇大喜，即令擊賊隨州，文詔追斬賊三百八十有奇。

translations.literal: Chengchou was greatly pleased and at once ordered an attack on the bandits at Suizhou; Wenzhao pursued and beheaded more than three hundred eighty bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou was delighted and sent him against the rebels at Suizhou; Wenzhao pursued and killed more than three hundred eighty of them.

sentences.zh: 四月，承疇次汝州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Chengchou encamped at Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Chengchou made camp at Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 以賊盡入關中，議還顧根本。

translations.literal: Because the bandits had all entered Guanzhong, they deliberated on returning to guard the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: With the rebels all in Guanzhong, they debated turning back to secure the base.

sentences.zh: 分命諸將扼要害，檄文詔入關，文詔乃馳至靈寶謁承疇。

translations.literal: They assigned the generals to hold the strategic points and summoned Wenzhao into the passes; Wenzhao then galloped to Lingbao to pay his respects to Chengchou.
translations.idiomatic: Generals were posted at key points and Wenzhao was summoned into the passes; he galloped to Lingbao to see Chengchou.

sentences.zh: 承疇以賊在商、雒，聞官兵至，必先走漢中，而大軍由潼關入，反在其後，乃令文詔由閿鄉取山路至雒南、商州，直搗賊巢，復從山陽、鎮安、洵陽馳入漢中，遏其奔軼。

translations.literal: Chengchou reasoned that with the bandits in Shang and Luo, on hearing government troops arrive they would first flee to Hanzhong, while the main army entering by Tong Pass would be behind them; he therefore ordered Wenzhao to take the mountain road from Wenxiang to Luonan and Shangzhou, strike straight at the bandit lair, then gallop from Shanyang, Zhen'an, and Xunyang into Hanzhong to block their flight.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou judged that rebels in Shang and Luo would flee to Hanzhong once they heard government troops were coming, leaving the main army entering through Tong Pass behind them. He ordered Wenzhao by mountain paths from Wenxiang to Luonan and Shangzhou to strike their lair, then through Shanyang, Zhen'an, and Xunyang into Hanzhong to cut off their escape.

sentences.zh: 曰：「此行也，道路回遠，將軍甚勞苦，吾集關中兵以待將軍。」

translations.literal: He said: "On this expedition the roads are long and circuitous; the general will suffer great hardship. I shall gather the Guanzhong troops to await the general."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "This march will be long and hard. I will gather the Guanzhong troops and wait for you."

sentences.zh: 拊其背而遣之，文詔跌馬去。

translations.literal: He clapped him on the back and sent him off; Wenzhao vaulted onto his horse and left.
translations.idiomatic: He clapped his back and sent him off; Wenzhao vaulted into the saddle and rode away.

sentences.zh: 五月五日抵商州。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the fifth month he reached Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the fifth month he reached Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊去城三十里，營火滿山。

translations.literal: The bandits were thirty li from the city; campfires covered the hills.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were thirty li from the city, their campfires covering the hills.

sentences.zh: 文詔夜半率從子參將變蛟、守備鼎蛟、都司白廣恩等敗賊深林中，追至金嶺川。

translations.literal: At midnight Wenzhao led his nephew the assistant general Bianjiao, the garrison commander Dingjiao, the regional commander Bai Guang'en, and others in defeating the bandits in the deep forest, pursuing to Jinling River.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight Wenzhao led his nephew Bianjiao, garrison commander Dingjiao, and regional commander Bai Guang'en into the forest, routed the rebels, and pursued them to Jinling River.

sentences.zh: 賊據險以千騎逆戰，變蛟大呼陷陣，諸軍並進，賊敗走。

translations.literal: The bandits held the heights with a thousand horsemen to meet them in battle; Bianjiao shouted and broke into their ranks, all the armies advanced together, and the bandits were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand rebel horsemen held the high ground; Bianjiao shouted and charged their lines, the whole force pressed forward, and the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 變蛟勇冠三軍，賊中聞大小曹將軍名，皆怖懾。

translations.literal: Bianjiao's bravery ranked first in the three armies; among the bandits, hearing the names of the great and little General Cao, all were struck with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Bianjiao's courage was unmatched in the army; among the rebels the names of the elder and younger General Cao inspired dread.

sentences.zh: 已而闖王、八大王諸賊犯鳳翔，趨汧陽、隴州，文詔自漢中馳赴。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits Rush-the-Sky King, Eight Great Kings, and others attacked Fengxiang and pressed toward Qianyang and Longzhou; Wenzhao galloped from Hanzhong to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Rush-the-Sky King, Eight Great Kings, and others struck Fengxiang and pressed toward Qianyang and Longzhou; Wenzhao galloped from Hanzhong to meet them.

sentences.zh: 賊盡向靜寧、泰安、清水、秦州間，眾且二十萬。

translations.literal: The bandits all turned toward the region among Jingning, Tai'an, Qingshui, and Qinzhou, their numbers nearing two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels converged on the country between Jingning, Tai'an, Qingshui, and Qinzhou, nearly two hundred thousand strong.

sentences.zh: 承疇以文詔所部合張全昌、張外嘉軍止六千，眾寡不敵，告急於朝，未得命。

translations.literal: Chengchou reckoned that Wenzhao's command together with Zhang Quanchang's and Zhang Waijia's armies amounted to only six thousand—too few to match the enemy—and reported urgently to the court, but received no orders.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou saw that Wenzhao, together with Zhang Quanchang and Zhang Waijia, had only six thousand men—far too few—and appealed urgently to court, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 六月，官軍遇賊亂馬川。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the government army met the bandits at Luanma River.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month government troops met the rebels at Luanma River.

sentences.zh: 前鋒中軍劉弘烈被執，俄副將艾萬年、柳國鎮復戰死。

translations.literal: The vanguard central commander Liu Honglie was captured; soon the deputy commanders Ai Wannian and Liu Guozhen again died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard commander Liu Honglie was taken prisoner; soon deputies Ai Wannian and Liu Guozhen were also killed.

sentences.zh: 文詔聞之，瞋目大罵，亟詣承疇請行。

translations.literal: When Wenzhao heard this, his eyes bulged and he cursed loudly; he hastened to Chengchou to ask leave to go.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Wenzhao glared and cursed; he hurried to Chengchou and asked to go at once.

sentences.zh: 承疇喜曰：「非將軍不能滅此賊。

translations.literal: Chengchou said with pleasure: "Without the general these bandits cannot be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou said gladly: "Only you can destroy these rebels.

sentences.zh: 顧吾兵已分，無可策應者。

translations.literal: Only my troops are already divided, and there is no one who can plan support.
translations.idiomatic: But my forces are already scattered, and I have none left to send in support.

sentences.zh: 將軍行，吾將由涇陽趨淳化為後勁。」

translations.literal: When the general goes, I shall hurry from Jingyang toward Chunhua as rear support."
translations.idiomatic: When you march, I will hurry from Jingyang toward Chunhua as your rear."

sentences.zh: 文詔乃以三千人自寧州進，遇賊真寧之湫頭鎮。

translations.literal: Wenzhao then advanced from Ningzhou with three thousand men and met the bandits at Qiutou Town in Zhenning.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao advanced from Ningzhou with three thousand men and met the rebels at Qiutou Town in Zhenning.

sentences.zh: 變蛟先登，斬首五百，追三十里，文詔率步兵繼之。

translations.literal: Bianjiao was first to ascend, beheaded five hundred, and pursued thirty li; Wenzhao led the foot soldiers after him.
translations.idiomatic: Bianjiao led the charge, took five hundred heads, and pursued thirty li; Wenzhao followed with the infantry.

sentences.zh: 賊伏數萬騎合圍，矢猬集。

translations.literal: Bandits lying in ambush with tens of thousands of horsemen closed in on all sides; arrows clustered thick as hedgehog quills.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of horsemen sprang from ambush and closed the ring; arrows fell thick as a hedgehog's quills.

sentences.zh: 賊不知為文詔也，有小卒縛急，大呼曰：「將軍救我！」

translations.literal: The bandits did not know it was Wenzhao; a young soldier, bound tight, cried loudly: "General, save me!"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did not yet know it was Wenzhao; a young soldier, bound tight, cried out: "General, save me!"

sentences.zh: 賊中叛卒識之，惎賊曰：「此曹總兵也。」

translations.literal: A defector among the bandits recognized him and incited the bandits, saying: "This is Commander Cao."
translations.idiomatic: A defector in the rebel ranks recognized him and cried: "This is Commander Cao!"

sentences.zh: 賊喜，圍益急。

translations.literal: The bandits rejoiced, and the encirclement grew tighter.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels rejoiced and pressed the ring tighter.

sentences.zh: 文詔左右跳蕩，手擊殺數十人，轉鬥數里。

translations.literal: Wenzhao leaped and fought on every side, killing dozens with his own hand, and battled for several li.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao fought on every side, killing dozens with his own hands, and battled for several li.

sentences.zh: 力不支，拔刀自刎死。

translations.literal: His strength failed; he drew his sword and cut his own throat to die.
translations.idiomatic: His strength gave out; he drew his sword and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 遊擊平安以下死者二十余人。

translations.literal: The guerrilla commander Ping An and more than twenty others below him died.
translations.idiomatic: Guerrilla commander Ping An and more than twenty officers died with him.

sentences.zh: 承疇聞，拊膺大哭，帝亦痛悼，贈太子太保、左都督，賜祭葬，世蔭指揮僉事，有司建祠，春秋致祭。

translations.literal: When Chengchou heard, he beat his breast and wept loudly; the emperor also grieved deeply, posthumously granting him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Chief Commander, bestowing sacrificial burial, hereditary enfeoffment as vice commander, ordering officials to build a shrine, and sacrifices in spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou beat his breast and wept; the emperor mourned him deeply, posthumously making him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Chief Commander, granting state burial and a hereditary vice commandership, and ordering a shrine with spring and autumn sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 文詔忠勇冠時，稱明季良將第一。

translations.literal: Wenzhao's loyalty and bravery ranked first in his age; he was called the foremost good general of the late Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao's loyalty and courage were unmatched in his day; he was called the finest general of the late Ming.

sentences.zh: 其死也，賊中為相慶。

translations.literal: At his death the bandits congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the rebels celebrated among themselves.

sentences.zh: 弟文耀，從兄征討，數有功。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wenyao followed his elder brother on campaigns and achieved merit many times.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wenyao campaigned with him and won merit repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 河曲之戰，斬獲多。

translations.literal: In the battle at Hequ, beheadings and captures were many.
translations.idiomatic: At Hequ he took many heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 後擊賊忻州，戰死城下。

translations.literal: Later, attacking bandits at Xinzhou, he died in battle below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Later, fighting rebels at Xinzhou, he was killed below the walls.

sentences.zh: 詔予贈恤。

translations.literal: An edict granted posthumous rewards and consolation.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 從子變蛟，自有傳。

translations.literal: His nephew Bianjiao has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Bianjiao has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 周遇吉，錦州衛人。

translations.literal: Zhou Yuji was a man of Jinzhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yuji was a native of Jinzhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 少有勇力，好射生。

translations.literal: In youth he had strength and courage and loved hunting.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was strong and bold and loved the hunt.

sentences.zh: 後入行伍，戰輒先登，積功至京營遊擊。

translations.literal: Later he entered the ranks; in battle he was always first to ascend, and through accumulated merit rose to guerrilla commander in the capital army.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered the army, was always first in the assault, and rose to guerrilla commander in the capital forces.

sentences.zh: 京營將多勛戚中官子弟，見遇吉質魯，意輕之。

translations.literal: The capital army generals were mostly sons of meritorious families and eunuchs; seeing Yuji's plain and rough manner, they looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Most capital commanders were sons of nobles and eunuchs; seeing Yuji's plain, rough manner, they looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 遇吉曰：「公等皆紈褲子，豈足當大敵。

translations.literal: Yuji said: "You gentlemen are all silk-trousered youths—how could you be equal to a great enemy?
translations.idiomatic: Yuji said: "You are all silk-pants dandies—how could you face a real enemy?

sentences.zh: 何不於無事時練膽勇，為異日用，而徒糜廩祿為！」

translations.literal: Why not in times of peace train courage and bravery for future use, instead of merely wasting grain salaries!"
translations.idiomatic: Why not train your courage in peacetime for the day it is needed, instead of wasting your rations!"

sentences.zh: 同輩鹹目笑之。

translations.literal: His comrades all eyed him and laughed.
translations.idiomatic: His comrades only eyed him and laughed.

sentences.zh: 崇禎九年，都城被兵。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chongzhen the capital was attacked by troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 9 the capital came under attack.

sentences.zh: 從尚書張鳳翼數血戰有功，連進二秩，為前鋒營副將。

translations.literal: Following the minister Zhang Fengyi he fought several bloody battles with merit, was promoted two ranks in succession, and became deputy commander of the vanguard camp.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Minister Zhang Fengyi he fought several bloody engagements with distinction, was promoted two ranks, and became deputy commander of the vanguard camp.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，從孫應元等討賊河南，戰光山、固始，皆大捷。

translations.literal: The next winter he followed Sun Yingyuan and others in campaigning against bandits in Henan, fighting at Guangshan and Gushi, all great victories.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter he joined Sun Yingyuan against Henan rebels and won major victories at Guangshan and Gushi.

sentences.zh: 十一年班師，進秩受賚。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the army returned; he was promoted in rank and received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the army returned; he was promoted and rewarded.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，復出討賊，破胡可受於淅川，降其全部。

translations.literal: The next autumn he again went out to campaign against bandits, defeated Hu Keshou at Xichuan, and accepted the surrender of his entire force.
translations.idiomatic: The next autumn he campaigned again, defeated Hu Keshou at Xichuan, and accepted the surrender of his whole band.

sentences.zh: 楊嗣昌出師襄陽，遇吉從中官劉元斌往會。

translations.literal: When Yang Sichang took the field at Xiangyang, Yuji followed the eunuch Liu Yuanbin to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Sichang marched from Xiangyang, Yuji went with eunuch Liu Yuanbin to join him.

sentences.zh: 會張獻忠將至房縣，嗣昌策其必窺渡鄖灘，遣遇吉扼守槐樹關，張一龍屯光化，賊遂不敢犯。

translations.literal: When Zhang Xianzhong was about to reach Fang County, Sichang judged that he would surely try to cross at Yutan Ford; he sent Yuji to hold Huai Tree Pass and Zhang Yilong to garrison Guanghua, and the bandits then did not dare attack.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhang Xianzhong approached Fang County, Sichang guessed he would try Yutan Ford; he posted Yuji at Huai Tree Pass and Zhang Yilong at Guanghua, and the rebels did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 十二月，獻忠敗於興安，將走竹山、竹溪，遇吉復以嗣昌令至石花街、草店扼其要害，賊自是盡入蜀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Xianzhong was defeated at Xing'an and was about to go toward Zhushan and Zhuxi; Yuji again by Sichang's order went to Shihua Street and Caodian to hold the strategic points, and from then on the bandits all entered Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Xianzhong was beaten at Xing'an and headed for Zhushan and Zhuxi; by Sichang's order Yuji blocked Shihua Street and Caodian, and the rebels thereafter poured into Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 遇吉乃從元斌駐荊門，專護獻陵。

translations.literal: Yuji then followed Yuanbin in garrisoning Jingmen, devoted solely to guarding the Xian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Yuji then garrisoned Jingmen with Yuanbin, charged solely with guarding the Xian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 明年與孫應元等大破羅汝才於豐邑坪。

translations.literal: The next year he and Sun Yingyuan and others utterly defeated Luo Rucai at Fengyi Plain.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he and Sun Yingyuan routed Luo Rucai at Fengyi Plain.

sentences.zh: 又明年與黃得功追破賊鳳陽。

translations.literal: The year after that he and Huang Degong pursued and defeated bandits at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he and Huang Degong pursued and defeated rebels at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 已而旋師，敗他賊李青山於壽張，追至東平，殲滅幾盡，青山遂降。

translations.literal: Before long the army returned; he defeated another bandit, Li Qingshan, at Shouzhang, pursued to Dongping, and nearly annihilated them; Qingshan then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The army then returned; he defeated Li Qingshan at Shouzhang, pursued him to Dongping, and nearly wiped out his band; Qingshan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 屢加太子少保、左都督。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Chief Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Chief Commander.

sentences.zh: 十五年冬，山西總兵官許定國有罪論死，以遇吉代之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifteenth year the Shanxi commander Xu Dingguo was found guilty and sentenced to death; Yuji was appointed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Chongzhen 15 Shanxi commander Xu Dingguo was sentenced to death for his crimes; Yuji replaced him.

sentences.zh: 至則汰老弱，繕甲仗，練勇敢，一軍特精。

translations.literal: On arriving he dismissed the old and weak, repaired armor and weapons, trained the brave, and the army became exceptionally elite.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he cut the old and weak, repaired arms and armor, drilled the brave, and made the army exceptionally sharp.

sentences.zh: 明年十二月，李自成陷全陜，將犯山西。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the next year Li Zicheng conquered all Shaanxi and was about to invade Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the following year Li Zicheng overran Shaanxi and prepared to invade Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 遇吉以沿河千餘里，賊處處可渡，分兵扼其上流，以下流蒲阪屬之巡撫蔡懋德，而請濟師於朝。

translations.literal: Yuji reasoned that along more than a thousand li of river the bandits could cross anywhere; he divided troops to hold the upper reaches and assigned the lower reaches at Puyuan to the grand coordinator Cai Maode, while requesting reinforcements from the court.
translations.idiomatic: Along more than a thousand li of river the rebels could cross anywhere; Yuji posted troops on the upper reaches, left the lower crossing at Puyuan to grand coordinator Cai Maode, and asked the court for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣副將熊通以二千人來赴。

translations.literal: The court sent the deputy commander Xiong Tong with two thousand men to come to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent deputy Xiong Tong with two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 十七年正月，遇吉令通防河。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year Yuji ordered Tong to defend the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Chongzhen 17 Yuji ordered Tong to guard the river.

sentences.zh: 會平陽守將陳尚智已遣使迎賊，諷通還鎮說降。

translations.literal: It happened that the Pingyang garrison commander Chen Shangzhi had already sent envoys to welcome the bandits and urged Tong to return to his post and persuade surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyang commander Chen Shangzhi had already sent envoys to welcome the rebels and urged Tong to return to camp and negotiate surrender.

sentences.zh: 遇吉叱之曰：「吾受國厚恩，寧從爾叛逆！

translations.literal: Yuji rebuked him, saying: "I have received great grace from the state—would I follow you in rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Yuji rebuked him: "The state has shown me great favor—would I join you in rebellion!

sentences.zh: 且爾統兵二千，不能殺賊，反作說客邪！」

translations.literal: Moreover you command two thousand troops and cannot kill bandits—instead you play the envoy!"
translations.idiomatic: You command two thousand men and cannot kill rebels—yet you play the envoy!"

sentences.zh: 立斬之，傳首京師。

translations.literal: He beheaded him on the spot and sent the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He executed him at once and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 至二月七日，太原陷，懋德死之。

translations.literal: By the seventh day of the second month Taiyuan fell and Maode died there.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the second month Taiyuan fell and Maode died defending it.

sentences.zh: 賊遂陷忻州，圍代州。

translations.literal: The bandits then captured Xinzhou and besieged Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then took Xinzhou and besieged Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 遇吉先在代遏其北犯，乃憑城固守，而潛出兵奮擊。

translations.literal: Yuji had first been at Daizhou blocking their northern advance; he then relied on the walls to hold firm while secretly sending troops out to strike fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Yuji had first blocked their northern advance at Daizhou; he then held the walls while secretly sallying out to strike hard.

sentences.zh: 連數日，殺賊無算。

translations.literal: For several days in succession they killed bandits beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: For days they killed rebels beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 會食盡援絕，退保寧武。

translations.literal: When food was exhausted and relief cut off, they withdrew to hold Ningwu.
translations.idiomatic: When provisions ran out and relief failed, they fell back to Ningwu.

sentences.zh: 賊亦踵至，大呼五日不降者屠其城。

translations.literal: The bandits also followed close behind, shouting that if they did not surrender within five days the city would be slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels followed close behind, shouting that anyone who did not surrender within five days would see the city massacred.

sentences.zh: 遇吉四面發大炮，殺賊萬人，火藥且盡，外圍轉急。

translations.literal: Yuji fired great cannon on all four sides, killing ten thousand bandits; gunpowder was nearly exhausted and the outer encirclement grew tighter.
translations.idiomatic: Yuji fired great guns on every side and killed ten thousand rebels; as powder ran low the ring closed tighter.

sentences.zh: 或請甘言紿之，遇吉怒曰：「若輩何怯邪！

translations.literal: Some asked to use sweet words to deceive them; Yuji said angrily: "Why are you people so cowardly!
translations.idiomatic: Some urged flattering words to deceive the enemy; Yuji snapped: "Why are you so afraid!

sentences.zh: 今能勝，一軍皆忠義。

translations.literal: If we can win now, the whole army will be loyal and righteous.
translations.idiomatic: If we win now, the whole army will be loyal and righteous.

sentences.zh: 即不支，縛我予賊。」

translations.literal: If we cannot hold, bind me and hand me to the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: If we cannot hold, bind me and hand me to the enemy."

sentences.zh: 於是設伏城內，出弱卒誘賊入城，亟下閘殺數千人。

translations.literal: He then set an ambush inside the city, sent out weak soldiers to lure the bandits into the city, and quickly lowered the gate bars, killing several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He laid an ambush inside the walls, sent weak troops to lure rebels in, then dropped the gates and killed several thousand.

sentences.zh: 賊用炮攻城，圮復完者再，傷其四驍將。

translations.literal: The bandits used cannon to attack the city; twice the walls were breached and repaired, and four of their fierce generals were wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels battered the walls with cannon; twice breaches were repaired, and four of their best generals were wounded.

sentences.zh: 自成懼，欲退。

translations.literal: Zicheng was afraid and wished to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng grew afraid and wanted to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 其將曰：「我眾百倍於彼，但用十攻一，番進，蔑不勝矣。」

translations.literal: His generals said: "Our numbers are a hundred times theirs; we need only use ten to attack one, advancing in rotation—how could we not win?"
translations.idiomatic: His generals said: "We outnumber them a hundredfold; send ten men for every one of theirs, rotate the assaults in waves, and we cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 自成從之。

translations.literal: Zicheng followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng agreed.

sentences.zh: 前隊死，後復繼。

translations.literal: The front ranks died and those behind continued.
translations.idiomatic: The front ranks died and those behind took their place.

sentences.zh: 官軍力盡，城遂陷。

translations.literal: The government army's strength was exhausted and the city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops were spent and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 遇吉巷戰，馬蹶，徒步跳蕩，手格殺數十人。

translations.literal: Yuji fought in the lanes; his horse stumbled, and on foot he leaped and fought, killing dozens with his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: Yuji fought in the lanes; his horse fell, and on foot he killed dozens with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 身被矢如猬，竟為賊執，大罵不屈。

translations.literal: His body was struck with arrows thick as a hedgehog; in the end he was captured by the bandits, cursed loudly, and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Arrows stuck in him thick as a hedgehog's quills; at last he was taken, cursed his captors, and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 賊懸之高竿，叢射殺之，復臠其肉。

translations.literal: The bandits hung him on a tall pole, shot him to death in a volley, and then carved up his flesh.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hung him on a tall pole, shot him to death, and carved up his flesh.

sentences.zh: 城中士民感遇吉忠義，巷戰殺賊，不可勝計。

translations.literal: The soldiers and people of the city, moved by Yuji's loyalty and righteousness, fought in the lanes and killed bandits beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by Yuji's loyalty, soldiers and civilians fought in the lanes and killed rebels beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 其舍中兒，先從遇吉出鬥，死亡略盡。

translations.literal: His household youths, who had first followed Yuji out to fight, were nearly all dead.
translations.idiomatic: The youths of his household who had marched out with him were nearly all dead.

sentences.zh: 夫人劉氏素勇健，率婦女數十人據山巔公廨，登屋而射，每一矢斃一賊，賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: His wife, Lady Liu, was by nature brave and strong; she led several dozen women to hold the public office on the hilltop, climbed the roof to shoot, and with each arrow killed one bandit; the bandits did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Liu was famously bold; she led several dozen women to the hilltop office, shot from the roof, and killed a rebel with every arrow; none dared come near.

sentences.zh: 縱火焚之，闔家盡死。

translations.literal: They set fire and burned them; the whole family perished.
translations.idiomatic: They set the building afire; the whole family died.

sentences.zh: 自成集眾計曰：「寧武雖破，吾將士死傷多。

translations.literal: Zicheng gathered his followers to deliberate, saying: "Although Ningwu is taken, my officers and soldiers have suffered many dead and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng gathered his commanders and said: "We have taken Ningwu, but my officers and men have suffered heavily.

sentences.zh: 自此達京師，歷大同、陽和、宣府、居庸，皆有重兵。

translations.literal: From here to the capital, passing Datong, Yanghe, Xuanfu, and Juyong, there are heavy troops everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: From here to the capital, through Datong, Yanghe, Xuanfu, and Juyong, every pass has strong garrisons.

sentences.zh: 倘盡如寧武，吾部下寧有孑遺哉！

translations.literal: If all were like Ningwu, would any of my followers survive!
translations.idiomatic: If every place fights like Ningwu, will any of my men survive!

sentences.zh: 不如還秦休息，圖後舉。」

translations.literal: It would be better to return to Qin to rest and plan a later campaign."
translations.idiomatic: Better to return to Qin, rest, and plan another campaign."

sentences.zh: 刻期將遁，而大同總兵姜襄降表至，自成大喜。

translations.literal: He set a date to flee, but the Datong commander Jiang Xiang's surrender memorial arrived, and Zicheng was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He set a date to withdraw, but Datong commander Jiang Xiang's surrender arrived, and Zicheng was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 方宴其使者，宣府總兵王承蔭表亦至，自成益喜。

translations.literal: While feasting his envoys, the Xuanfu commander Wang Chengyin's surrender memorial also arrived, and Zicheng was still more pleased.
translations.idiomatic: While entertaining their envoys, Xuanfu commander Wang Chengyin's surrender arrived as well, and Zicheng rejoiced all the more.

sentences.zh: 遂決策長驅，歷大同、宣府抵居庸。

translations.literal: He then resolved on a long drive, passing through Datong and Xuanfu to reach Juyong.
translations.idiomatic: He then decided to march straight through Datong and Xuanfu to Juyong.

sentences.zh: 太監杜之秩、總兵唐通復開門延之，京師遂不守矣。

translations.literal: The eunuch Du Zhiji and the commander Tang Tong again opened the gates to welcome them, and the capital could no longer be held.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Du Zhiji and commander Tang Tong opened the gates to them, and the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 賊每語人曰：「他鎮復有一周總兵，吾安得至此。」

translations.literal: The bandits often said to people: "If every garrison had another Commander Zhou, how could we have reached here?"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels often said: "If every pass had another Commander Zhou, how could we have come this far?"

sentences.zh: 福王時，贈太保，謚忠武，列祀旌忠祠。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian, given the posthumous title Loyal Martial, and enshrined in the Shrine of Loyal Merit.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously made Grand Guardian, given the title Loyal Martial, and enshrined in the Shrine of Loyal Merit.

sentences.zh: 黃得功，號虎山，開原衛人，其先自合肥徙。

translations.literal: Huang Degong, styled Hushan, was a man of Kaiyuan Guard; his ancestors had moved from Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Degong, styled Tiger Mountain, was a native of Kaiyuan Guard; his family had moved from Hefei.

sentences.zh: 早孤，與母徐居。

translations.literal: He lost his father early and lived with his mother, Lady Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he lived with his mother, Lady Xu.

sentences.zh: 少負奇氣，膽略過人。

translations.literal: In youth he possessed extraordinary spirit; his courage and daring surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he had an uncommon spirit and courage beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 年十二，母釀酒熟，竊飲至盡。

translations.literal: At twelve his mother brewed wine until it was ripe; he stole and drank it all.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he drank all the wine his mother had brewed.

sentences.zh: 母責之，笑曰：「償易耳。」

translations.literal: His mother scolded him; he laughed and said: "Repayment is easy."
translations.idiomatic: His mother scolded him; he laughed and said: "That's easy to repay."

sentences.zh: 時遼事急，得功持刀雜行伍中，出斬首二級，中賞率得白金五十兩，歸奉母，曰：「兒以償酒也。」

translations.literal: At that time the Liaodong crisis was urgent; Degong took a blade and mingled among the ranks, went out and beheaded two men, won the standard reward of fifty taels of white silver, returned and presented it to his mother, saying: "Your son repays the wine."
translations.idiomatic: With the Liaodong crisis urgent, he took a blade, joined the ranks, brought back two heads, won the standard fifty taels of silver, gave them to his mother, and said: "I've repaid the wine."

sentences.zh: 由是隸經略為親軍，累功至遊擊。

translations.literal: From this he entered the commissioner-general's personal guard and through accumulated merit rose to guerrilla commander.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the commissioner-general's personal guard and rose to guerrilla commander.

sentences.zh: 崇禎九年，遷副總兵，分管京衛管。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chongzhen he was transferred to deputy commander and placed in charge of the capital guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 9 he became deputy commander in charge of the capital guard.

sentences.zh: 十一年以禁軍從總督熊文燦擊賊於舞陽，鏖光、固間，最。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he led the forbidden army following the governor-general Xiong Wencan to attack bandits at Wuyang, fighting fiercely between Guangshan and Gushi; his merit ranked foremost.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he led the imperial guard with governor-general Xiong Wencan against rebels at Wuyang and fought fiercest between Guangshan and Gushi.

sentences.zh: 八月又從擊賊馬光玉於淅川之吳村、王家寨，大破之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he again followed in attacking the bandit Ma Guangyu at Wucun and Wangjia Stockade in Xichuan and utterly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he again joined the attack on Ma Guangyu at Wucun and Wangjia Stockade in Xichuan and routed him.

sentences.zh: 詔加太子太師，署總兵銜。

translations.literal: An edict added the title Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and gave him acting commander rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent with acting commander rank.

sentences.zh: 十三年從太監盧九德破賊於板石畈，賊革裹眼等五營降。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he followed the eunuch Lu Jiude in defeating bandits at Banshi Plain; five camps including Leather-Wrapped Eye surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he followed eunuch Lu Jiude in defeating rebels at Banshi Plain; five camps including Leather-Wrapped Eye surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十四年以總兵與王憲分護鳳陽、泗州陵，得功駐定遠。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, as commander he and Wang Xian jointly guarded the Fengyang and Sizhou mausoleums; Degong garrisoned Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he and Wang Xian guarded the Fengyang and Sizhou mausoleums as commanders; Degong was posted at Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 張獻忠攻桐城，挾營將廖應登至城下誘降。

translations.literal: Zhang Xianzhong attacked Tongcheng, bringing the camp officer Liao Yingdeng to the foot of the walls to induce surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong attacked Tongcheng and brought camp officer Liao Yingdeng to the walls to urge surrender.

sentences.zh: 得功與劉良佐合兵擊之於鮑家嶺，賊敗遁，追至潛山，擒斬賊將闖世王馬武、三鷂子王興國。

translations.literal: Degong and Liu Liangzuo combined forces and struck them at Baojia Ridge; the bandits were defeated and fled; pursuing to Qianshan, they captured and beheaded the bandit generals Rush-the-World King Ma Wu and Three-Hawks Wang Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Degong and Liu Liangzuo struck them at Baojia Ridge; the rebels fled; at Qianshan they captured and killed Rush-the-World King Ma Wu and Three-Hawks Wang Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 三鷂子，獻忠養子，最號驍勇者也。

translations.literal: Three-Hawks was Xianzhong's adopted son and was called the fiercest and bravest.
translations.idiomatic: Three-Hawks was Xianzhong's adopted son and the fiercest of his fighters.

sentences.zh: 得功箭傷面，愈自奮，與賊轉戰十余日，所殺傷獨多。

translations.literal: Degong was wounded in the face by an arrow but fought all the harder; he battled the bandits for more than ten days and alone killed and wounded the most.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow struck his face, but he fought all the harder; for more than ten days he battled the rebels and killed more than any other.

sentences.zh: 明年移鎮廬州。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to garrison Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 十七年封靖南伯。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was enfeoffed as Marquis Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 17 he was made Marquis Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 福王立江南，進封侯。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu established himself south of the Yangtze, Degong was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu ruled south of the Yangtze, he was promoted to marquis.

sentences.zh: 旋命與劉良佐、劉澤清、高傑為四鎮。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered, together with Liu Liangzuo, Liu Zeqing, and Gao Jie, to form the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named one of the Four Garrisons with Liu Liangzuo, Liu Zeqing, and Gao Jie.

sentences.zh: 初，督輔史可法慮傑跋扈難制，故置得功儀真，陰相牽制。

translations.literal: At first the supervising minister Shi Kefa feared Jie's overbearing manner was hard to control, and therefore stationed Degong at Yizhen to restrain him covertly.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising minister Shi Kefa feared Gao Jie's arrogance and stationed Degong at Yizhen to check him.

sentences.zh: 適登萊總兵黃蜚將之任，蜚與得功同姓，稱兄弟，移書請兵備非常。

translations.literal: It happened that the Denglai commander Huang Fei was about to take up his post; Fei shared Degong's surname and called him brother, sending a letter requesting extraordinary military preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Denglai commander Huang Fei was about to take office; he shared Degong's surname, called him brother, and asked for extra troops.

sentences.zh: 得功率騎三百由揚州往高郵迎之，傑副將胡茂楨馳報傑。

translations.literal: Degong led three hundred horsemen from Yangzhou toward Gaoyou to welcome him; Jie's deputy Hu Maozhen galloped to report to Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Degong led three hundred horsemen from Yangzhou to Gaoyou to meet him; Gao Jie's deputy Hu Maozhen rode to warn Jie.

sentences.zh: 傑素忌得功，又疑圖己，乃伏精卒道中，邀擊之。

translations.literal: Jie had long envied Degong and also suspected a plot against himself; he therefore hid elite troops along the road and ambushed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jie had long resented Degong and suspected a plot; he hid elite troops along the road and ambushed him.

sentences.zh: 得功行至土橋，方作食，伏起，出不意，上馬舉鐵鞭，飛矢雨集，馬踣，騰他騎馳。

translations.literal: Degong reached Tuqiao and was just taking a meal when the ambush rose; caught unawares, he mounted, raised his iron whip, arrows fell like rain, his horse fell, and he leaped onto another horse and galloped off.
translations.idiomatic: At Tuqiao Degong was eating when the ambush sprang up; he mounted, raised his iron whip, arrows fell like rain, his horse went down, and he leaped to another horse and fled.

sentences.zh: 有驍騎舞槊直前，得功大呼，反鬥，挾其槊而抶之，人馬皆糜。

translations.literal: A fierce horseman danced his lance straight forward; Degong shouted loudly, turned to fight, seized the lance and struck with it, and both man and horse were pulverized.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce rider charged with his lance; Degong shouted, turned, seized the lance, and struck—rider and horse were smashed.

sentences.zh: 復殺數十人，跳入頹垣中，哮聲如雷，追者不敢進，遂疾馳至大軍，得免。

translations.literal: He killed several dozen more, leaped into a ruined wall, roared like thunder, and the pursuers did not dare advance; he then galloped swiftly to the main army and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He killed dozens more, leaped into a ruined wall, and roared like thunder until pursuers dared not come near; he galloped back to the main force and escaped.

sentences.zh: 方鬥時，傑潛師搗儀真，得功兵頗傷，而所俱行三百騎皆歿。

translations.literal: While he was fighting, Jie secretly sent troops to strike Yizhen; Degong's soldiers suffered considerable losses, and all three hundred horsemen who had accompanied him perished.
translations.idiomatic: While he fought, Jie secretly struck Yizhen; Degong's men were badly hurt, and all three hundred horsemen with him were killed.

sentences.zh: 遂訴於朝，願與傑決一死戰。

translations.literal: He then appealed to the court, wishing to fight Jie to the death.
translations.idiomatic: He appealed to court, demanding a fight to the death with Jie.

sentences.zh: 可法命監軍萬元吉和解之，不可。

translations.literal: Kefa ordered the supervising general Wan Yuanji to mediate a settlement, but it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa sent supervising general Wan Yuanji to mediate, but Degong would not agree.

sentences.zh: 會得功有母喪，可法來吊，語之曰：「土橋之役，無智愚皆知傑不義。

translations.literal: It happened that Degong was in mourning for his mother; Kefa came to offer condolences and said to him: "In the affair at Tuqiao, wise and foolish alike know Jie was unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Degong was mourning his mother; Kefa came to condole and said: "Everyone knows Jie was wrong at Tuqiao.

sentences.zh: 今將軍以國故捐盛怒，而歸曲於高，是將軍收大名於天下也。」

translations.literal: Now if the general for the state's sake sets aside great anger and lays the fault on Gao, this is how the general will win great renown under heaven."
translations.idiomatic: If you set aside your anger for the state's sake and lay the blame on Gao, you will win great renown throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 得功色稍和，終以所殺亡多為恨。

translations.literal: Degong's expression softened somewhat, but in the end he still resented the many killed and lost.
translations.idiomatic: Degong's face softened, but he still grieved the many dead.

sentences.zh: 可法令傑償其馬，復出千金為母赗。

translations.literal: Kefa ordered Jie to compensate his horses and also gave a thousand gold for his mother's funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa made Jie pay for his horses and gave a thousand gold for his mother's funeral.

sentences.zh: 得功不得已，聽之。

translations.literal: Degong had no choice and acquiesced.
translations.idiomatic: Degong had no choice but to accept.

sentences.zh: 明年，傑欲趨河南，規取中原。

translations.literal: The next year Jie wished to hurry to Henan and plan the recovery of the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Jie planned to march to Henan and recover the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 詔得功與劉良佐守邳、徐。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Degong and Liu Liangzuo to guard Pi and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Degong and Liu Liangzuo were ordered to guard Pi and Xu.

sentences.zh: 傑死，得功還儀真。

translations.literal: When Jie died, Degong returned to Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Jie died, Degong returned to Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 傑家並將士妻子尚留揚州，得功謀襲之。

translations.literal: Jie's family and the wives and children of his officers and soldiers still remained in Yangzhou; Degong planned to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Jie's family and his officers' wives and children were still in Yangzhou; Degong planned to attack them.

sentences.zh: 朝廷急遣盧九德諭止，得功遂移鎮廬州。

translations.literal: The court urgently sent Lu Jiude to admonish and stop him; Degong then transferred his garrison to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Lu Jiude to stop him; Degong then moved his garrison to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 四月，左良玉東下，以請君側為名，至九江，病死，軍中立其子夢庚。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Zuo Liangyu marched east under the pretext of removing evil from the ruler's side; reaching Jiujiang, he died of illness, and the army set up his son Menggeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Zuo Liangyu marched east on the pretext of purging the court; he died at Jiujiang, and the army made his son Menggeng commander.

sentences.zh: 命得功趨上江禦之，駐師荻港。

translations.literal: Degong was ordered to hurry upriver to resist them and encamped at Digang.
translations.idiomatic: Degong was ordered upriver to oppose them and encamped at Digang.

sentences.zh: 得功破夢庚於銅陵，解其圍。

translations.literal: Degong defeated Menggeng at Tongling and lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Degong defeated Menggeng at Tongling and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 命移家鎮太平，一意辦賊，論功加左柱國。

translations.literal: He was ordered to move his household and garrison to Taiping, devote himself solely to dealing with bandits, and for his merit was given the additional title of Left Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his household to Taiping, devoted himself to fighting rebels, and was made Left Pillar of State for his merit.

sentences.zh: 時大清兵已渡江，知福王奔，分兵襲太平。

translations.literal: At this time the Great Qing army had already crossed the Yangtze; learning that the Prince of Fu had fled, they divided troops to attack Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing army had crossed the Yangtze; learning the Prince of Fu had fled, they sent detachments against Taiping.

sentences.zh: 得功方收兵屯蕪湖，福王潛入其營。

translations.literal: Degong was just gathering his troops and encamping at Wuhu when the Prince of Fu secretly entered his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Degong was gathering his troops at Wuhu when the Prince of Fu slipped into his camp.

sentences.zh: 得功驚泣曰：「陛下死守京城，臣等猶可盡力，奈何聽奸人言，倉卒到此！

translations.literal: Degong said in shock and tears: "Your Majesty should have held the capital to the death; we could still have done our utmost—why listen to wicked men's words and come here in such haste!
translations.idiomatic: Degong cried in shock: "Your Majesty should have held the capital to the death—we could still have fought—why listen to villains and flee here in such haste!

sentences.zh: 且臣方對敵，安能扈駕？」

translations.literal: Moreover your servant is facing the enemy—how can he escort the imperial carriage?"
translations.idiomatic: And I am facing the enemy—how can I escort Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 王曰：「非卿無可仗者。」

translations.literal: The prince said: "Without you there is no one to rely on."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said: "There is no one else I can rely on."

sentences.zh: 得功泣曰：「願效死。」

translations.literal: Degong wept and said: "I wish to give my life in service."
translations.idiomatic: Degong wept and said: "I will die for you."

sentences.zh: 得功戰荻港時，傷臂幾墮。

translations.literal: When Degong fought at Digang his arm was wounded and nearly severed.
translations.idiomatic: At Digang his arm was wounded nearly to the point of falling off.

sentences.zh: 衣葛衣，以帛絡臂，佩刀坐小舟，督麾下八總兵結束前迎敵。

translations.literal: He wore hempen clothes, bound his arm with silk, wore his sword, sat in a small boat, and directed his eight commanders to array themselves and advance to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He wore plain hemp, bound his arm with silk, sword at his side, sat in a small boat, and sent his eight commanders forward to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 而劉良佐已先歸命，大呼岸上招降。

translations.literal: But Liu Liangzuo had already surrendered first and shouted loudly from the shore inviting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: But Liu Liangzuo had already surrendered and shouted from the shore urging them to yield.

sentences.zh: 得功怒叱曰：「汝乃降乎！」

translations.literal: Degong rebuked him angrily: "Have you surrendered!"
translations.idiomatic: Degong roared: "You have surrendered!"

sentences.zh: 忽飛矢至，中其喉偏左。

translations.literal: Suddenly a flying arrow came and struck him slightly left of the throat.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow struck him just left of the throat.

sentences.zh: 得功知不可為，擲刀拾所拔箭刺吭死。

translations.literal: Degong knew nothing could be done; he threw down his sword, picked up the arrow he had pulled out, and stabbed himself in the throat to die.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing all was lost, he threw down his sword, took the arrow he had pulled out, and drove it into his throat.

sentences.zh: 其妻聞之，亦自經。

translations.literal: When his wife heard, she also hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: His wife heard and hanged herself as well.

sentences.zh: 總兵翁之琪投江死，中軍田雄遂挾福王降。
