translations.literal: The commander Weng Zhiqi threw himself into the river and died; the central commander Tian Xiong then seized the Prince of Fu and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Weng Zhiqi drowned himself in the river; central commander Tian Xiong seized the Prince of Fu and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 得功粗猛不識文義。

translations.literal: Degong was rough and fierce and did not understand literary meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Degong was rough and fierce and barely literate.

sentences.zh: 江南初立，王詔書指揮，多出群小。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was first established, the prince's edicts and commands mostly came from petty men.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern regime was first set up, the prince's orders mostly came from petty men at court.

sentences.zh: 得功得詔紙或對使罵裂之。

translations.literal: When Degong received an edict he sometimes cursed at the envoy and tore it apart.
translations.idiomatic: When he received an edict he sometimes cursed the messenger and tore it up.

sentences.zh: 然忠義出天性，聞以國事相規誡者，輒屈己改不旋踵。

translations.literal: Yet loyalty and righteousness came from his nature; when he heard admonition on state affairs, he would humble himself and reform without turning back.
translations.idiomatic: Yet loyalty was in his nature; when admonished on matters of state, he humbled himself and changed at once.

sentences.zh: 北來太子之獄，得功抗疏爭曰：「東宮未必假冒，先帝子即上子，未有了無證明，混然雷同者。

translations.literal: In the case of the crown prince brought from the north, Degong submitted a defiant memorial arguing: "The Eastern Palace is not necessarily a counterfeit; the former emperor's son is the present emperor's son. There is no case without any proof at all in which all are confusedly taken to agree.
translations.idiomatic: In the case of the crown prince brought from the north, Degong submitted a forceful memorial: "The heir apparent may not be a fake; the late emperor's son is the present emperor's son. No case lacks all proof yet ends in unanimous agreement.

sentences.zh: 臣恐在廷諸臣，諂徇者多，抗顏者少，即明白識認，亦不敢抗詞取禍矣。」

translations.literal: Your servant fears that among the court ministers many flatter and comply while few speak with defiant faces; even if they clearly recognize the truth, they dare not speak against it and invite disaster."
translations.idiomatic: I fear too many at court flatter while too few speak plainly; even those who know the truth dare not contradict and invite disaster."

sentences.zh: 時太子真偽莫敢決，而得功忠憤不阿如此。

translations.literal: At that time none dared decide whether the crown prince was genuine or false, yet Degong's loyal indignation refused to yield in this way.
translations.idiomatic: None dared decide whether the prince was genuine, yet Degong's loyal anger would not bend.

sentences.zh: 得功每戰，飲酒數鬥，酒酣氣益厲。

translations.literal: Before each battle Degong drank several dou of wine; when the wine was warm his spirit grew fiercer still.
translations.idiomatic: Before each battle he drank several dou of wine; when warmed by drink his spirit grew fiercer.

sentences.zh: 喜持鐵鞭戰，鞭漬血沾手腕，以水濡之，久乃得脫，軍中呼為黃闖子。

translations.literal: He loved to fight with an iron whip; when blood soaked the whip and stuck to his wrist, he wet it with water and only after a long time could he pull free; the army called him Yellow Charger.
translations.idiomatic: He fought with an iron whip; when blood glued it to his wrist he had to soak it in water before he could pull free—the army called him Yellow Charger.

sentences.zh: 始為偏裨，隨大帥立功名，未嘗一當大敵。

translations.literal: At first he was a junior officer following great commanders in winning fame and merit, and had never once faced a great enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a junior officer under great commanders and had never faced a major enemy alone.

sentences.zh: 及專鎮封侯，不及一年余而南北轉徙，主逃將潰，無所一用其力，束手就殪，與國俱亡而已。

translations.literal: When he came to hold his own command and was enfeoffed as marquis, in little more than a year he shifted north and south; the ruler fled, generals collapsed, there was nowhere to use his strength once, he was bound hand and foot and slaughtered, and perished with the state—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held independent command and a marquisate, in little more than a year the court fled south, armies collapsed, he had no chance to use his strength, and was cut down with the state.

sentences.zh: 其軍行紀律嚴，下無敢犯，所至人感其德。

translations.literal: His army on the march was strictly disciplined; none below dared violate it, and wherever he went people were moved by his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His army marched under strict discipline; none dared offend, and people everywhere were moved by his virtue.

sentences.zh: 廬州、桐城、定遠皆為立生祠。

translations.literal: Luzhou, Tongcheng, and Dingyuan all erected living shrines to him.
translations.idiomatic: Living shrines were built to him in Luzhou, Tongcheng, and Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 葬儀真方山母墓側。

translations.literal: He was buried at Yizhen on Mount Fang beside his mother's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at Yizhen on Mount Fang beside his mother's grave.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：曹文詔等秉驍猛之資，所向摧敗，皆所稱萬人敵也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Cao Wenzhao and the others possessed fierce and valiant gifts; wherever they turned they crushed defeat, and all were called match for ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Cao Wenzhao and his peers were fierce by nature; wherever they turned they shattered the enemy, and each was called a match for ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 大命既傾，良將顛蹶。

translations.literal: When the great mandate had already toppled, good generals stumbled and fell.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty's mandate had already collapsed, good generals fell with it.

sentences.zh: 三人者忠勇最著，死事亦最烈，故別著於篇。

translations.literal: These three men's loyalty and bravery were most outstanding, and their deaths in service were also most fierce; therefore they are set forth separately in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: These three were the most loyal and brave, and died the most fiercely in service; therefore they are given a chapter of their own.
